extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: MMMU is a new benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators collected multimodal questions from textbooks and online resources, and created new questions based on their expertise. Quality control involved three stages: 1) identifying duplicates using lexical overlap and URL similarity, 2) manual format and typo checking by co-authors, and 3) categorizing problems into four difficulty levels and excluding overly simplistic ones.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students, including the paper's co-authors, who specialize in the majors/subjects covered by the benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process of the dataset may introduce biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark's focus on college-level subjects may not be sufficient for fully testing Expert AGI, and the manual curation process may carry biases.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark helps monitor progress towards Expert AGI, which has significant societal implications including potential job displacement and economic disruption.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed as a benchmark to evaluate multimodal models on multi-discipline tasks. It is divided into development, validation, and test sets, and is intended for zero-shot or few-shot evaluation rather than fine-tuning.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset was split into a few-shot development set, a validation set, and a test set.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data cleaning involved identifying and eliminating duplicate problems using lexical overlap and source URL similarity, standardizing formats, correcting typos, and filtering out approximately 10% of the problems that were classified as 'very easy'.

MMMU , constituting 11.5K questions, is divided into a few-shot development set, a validation set, and a test set. ... Our evaluation is conducted under a zero-shot setting to assess the capability of models to generate accurate answers without fine-tuning or few-shot demonstrations on our benchmark.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: MMMU, constituting 11.5K questions, is divided into a few-shot development set, a validation set, and a test set. The few-shot development set includes 5 questions per subject, and the validation set, useful for hyperparameter selection, contains approximately 900 questions, while the test set comprises 10.5K questions.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: To further control the quality of our data, we perform two steps of data cleaning. In the first stage, lexical overlap and source URL similarity are employed to identify potential duplicate problems. These suspected duplicates were then reviewed by the authors to identify and eliminate any duplications. The second stage involves distributing the problems among different co-authors for format and typo checking. This step requires authors to ensure adherence to a standardized format, undertaking necessary corrections where deviations are found. In the third and final stage... Approximately 10% of the problems, classified as very easy and not aligning with our design criteria due to their simplistic nature, are excluded from the benchmark.
